verdict.rationale: Kushki documents its own 'Kajita de pagos', described as a customizable payment form, and a JS library (kushki.js, also used for 3DS integration). These are presented separately from the 'Botón de pagos', which explicitly redirects to a hosted portal, so they point to an on-site, non-redirect option. The evidence is only titles and taglines, so in-page embedding and the depth of customization are implied rather than documented. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that Kajita or kushki.js components embed directly in the merchant's site or app, details of the customization options (styling, fields, layout), mobile/app SDK support, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed customizable payment components directly in my own site or app instead of redirecting to a hosted page
